STUDY 01 / 10 BRIEF CASE 02

Progressive Electricity Billing

Slabs · conditions · comparisons6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Calculate household electricity bills using progressive consumption slabs, a fixed charge, a surcharge, and an on-time rebate. Compare a chronological sequence of monthly bills, identify increases greater than a specified threshold, and report every month tied for the highest bill.

02 Objectives

  • Apply progressive slabs without charging all units at the highest rate.
  • Use conditional rules for surcharge, rebate, and unusual bill increases.
  • Store monthly records as tuples in a list and unpack them during processing.
  • Preserve exact paise amounts while calculating and rounding charges.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: separate input validation, energy slabs, adjustments, and trend reporting.
  • Pattern recognition: each month follows the same tariff calculation.
  • Abstraction: represent a month by only its label, consumption, and on-time flag.
  • Algorithm design: scan the chronological list once, keeping the previous bill and the running maximum.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • The supplied brief gives no tariff values. The following rates are classroom assumptions, not an electricity provider's tariff.
  • Accept 1-12 months in chronological order, with unique labels of 1-12 characters. Labels are compared without regard to case. Units are nonnegative whole kWh.
  • The first 100 units cost Rs 1.50 each, the next 100 cost Rs 2.50 each, and every unit above 200 costs Rs 4.00. Fixed charge: Rs 50.00 per month, including at zero consumption.
  • Consumption above 300 units incurs a surcharge of 10% of the energy charge. At 100 units or less, on-time payment earns a rebate of 5% of the energy charge.
  • Money is calculated in integer paise. Percentage charges are rounded half up to the nearest paise using (amount * rate + 50) // 100. Only display formatting converts to rupees.
  • An unusual increase is strictly greater than 25% of the preceding final bill. Exactly 25% does not trigger an alert. There is no alert for the first month.
  • Malformed month records are retried and do not consume a month slot. Highest-bill ties retain input order.

INPUT CONTRACT

First enter the month count. Then enter label|units|Y/N for each month. Y means payment by the due date. Example: Jan|100|Y.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

An itemized monthly bill, percentage change from the preceding month, alert labels, total billed amount, and all highest-bill month labels.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read and validate the month count.
  2. Read each three-field record. Validate the label, units, and Y/N flag; retry invalid or duplicate records.
  3. Store accepted records as (label, units, on_time) tuples.
  4. For each month, calculate energy in paise using the three progressive slabs.
  5. Calculate the applicable surcharge and rebate, round each to paise, and add the fixed charge.
  6. Print the bill. From the second month onward, calculate percentage change and flag bill * 100 > previous_bill * 125.
  7. Accumulate the grand total and maintain the highest bill and every tied label.
  8. Print the total, highest-bill labels, and unusual-increase labels.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ a valid month_count in 1..12
months <- empty list; labels <- empty list
WHILE accepted months < month_count
    READ label, units, on_time
    IF record is invalid OR label already exists
        PRINT error; RETRY
    ELSE
        APPEND (label, units, on_time) to months
        APPEND normalized label to labels
previous_bill <- 0; highest_bill <- -1; total <- 0
FOR EACH (label, units, on_time) IN months
    IF units <= 100
        energy <- units * 150
    ELSE IF units <= 200
        energy <- 15000 + (units - 100) * 250
    ELSE
        energy <- 40000 + (units - 200) * 400
    surcharge <- 0; rebate <- 0
    IF units > 300: surcharge <- (energy * 10 + 50) DIV 100
    IF units <= 100 AND on_time = Y
        rebate <- (energy * 5 + 50) DIV 100
    bill <- energy + 5000 + surcharge - rebate
    PRINT itemized bill
    IF previous_bill > 0
        PRINT (bill - previous_bill) * 100 / previous_bill
        IF bill * 100 > previous_bill * 125: RECORD alert
    UPDATE highest bill and all ties
    total <- total + bill; previous_bill <- bill
PRINT total, highest-bill months, alert months
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 02_electricity_billing/program.py
Read the complete program 76 lines · no imports
print("PROGRESSIVE ELECTRICITY BILLING")
print("Enter months in chronological order: label|units|on_time(Y/N)")

month_count_text = input("Number of months (1-12): ").strip()
while not month_count_text.isascii() or not month_count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(month_count_text) <= 12:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 12.")
    month_count_text = input("Number of months (1-12): ").strip()
month_count = int(month_count_text)

months = []
labels = []
while len(months) < month_count:
    fields = input(f"Month {len(months) + 1}: ").split("|")
    if len(fields) != 3:
        print("ERROR: expected label|units|Y/N.")
        continue
    label, units_text, on_time = fields
    label = label.strip()
    units_text = units_text.strip()
    on_time = on_time.strip().upper()
    if not 1 <= len(label) <= 12 or label.lower() in labels:
        print("ERROR: month labels must be nonempty, unique, and at most 12 characters.")
        continue
    if not units_text.isascii() or not units_text.isdigit():
        print("ERROR: units must be a nonnegative whole number.")
        continue
    if on_time not in ("Y", "N"):
        print("ERROR: on-time payment must be Y or N.")
        continue
    months.append((label, int(units_text), on_time))
    labels.append(label.lower())

print("\nBILL DETAILS (Rs)")
print("Month | Units | Energy | Fixed | Surcharge | Rebate | Total")
previous_bill = 0
highest_bill = -1
highest_months = []
unusual_months = []
grand_total = 0

for label, units, on_time in months:
    if units <= 100:
        energy = units * 150
    elif units <= 200:
        energy = 100 * 150 + (units - 100) * 250
    else:
        energy = 100 * 150 + 100 * 250 + (units - 200) * 400
    fixed = 5000
    surcharge = 0
    rebate = 0
    if units > 300:
        surcharge = (energy * 10 + 50) // 100
    if units <= 100 and on_time == "Y":
        rebate = (energy * 5 + 50) // 100
    bill = energy + fixed + surcharge - rebate
    grand_total += bill
    print(f"{label} | {units} | {energy / 100:.2f} | {fixed / 100:.2f} | {surcharge / 100:.2f} | {rebate / 100:.2f} | {bill / 100:.2f}")
    if previous_bill > 0:
        change = (bill - previous_bill) * 100 / previous_bill
        print(f"  Change from previous month: {change:+.2f}%")
        if bill * 100 > previous_bill * 125:
            unusual_months.append(label)
            print("  ALERT: bill increase exceeds 25%.")
    if bill > highest_bill:
        highest_bill = bill
        highest_months = [label]
    elif bill == highest_bill:
        highest_months.append(label)
    previous_bill = bill

print(f"Total billed: Rs {grand_total / 100:.2f}")
print(f"Highest bill: Rs {highest_bill / 100:.2f} ({', '.join(highest_months)})")
if len(unusual_months) == 0:
    print("Unusual increases: none")
else:
    print(f"Unusual increases: {', '.join(unusual_months)}")

10 Conclusion

The solution combines progressive arithmetic, conditional policies, and a running comparison without advanced Python features. Its boundary tests distinguish slab transitions, the 300-unit surcharge threshold, paise rounding, and an increase of exactly 25%.

STUDY 02 / 10 BRIEF CASE 13

ATM Transaction Sequence Simulation

State · validation · reconciliation6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Simulate a sequence of deposits and withdrawals against one account. Validate each attempted transaction, enforce withdrawal limits and a minimum balance, leave balances unchanged for rejected attempts, and produce a transaction-by-transaction audit and final reconciliation.

02 Objectives

  • Maintain an account balance across a sequential transaction list.
  • Apply multiple validation and withdrawal conditions in a defined order.
  • Reject repeated transaction identifiers without double-processing an amount.
  • Reconcile the opening balance, deposits, withdrawals, and closing balance.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate setup, identify transactions, apply account rules, and reconcile.
  • Pattern recognition: every accepted transaction changes the same balance state.
  • Abstraction: retain identifiers, operation types, amounts, and resulting balances.
  • Algorithm design: process in input order because earlier operations affect later eligibility.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • This is a one-day classroom simulation using fictional data and whole rupees. It does not connect to a bank.
  • Opening balance is at least Rs 500. Accept 1-50 attempted transactions. Deposits have no policy cap and must be positive whole rupees.
  • Withdrawal amounts must be positive multiples of Rs 100, no more than Rs 10000 per transaction, and no more than Rs 20000 in successful withdrawals during the day.
  • Every successful withdrawal must leave at least Rs 500. A later deposit does not reset the daily withdrawal allowance.
  • A transaction ID is 1-12 ASCII letters or digits, normalized to uppercase. A well-formed row with a syntactically valid new ID reserves that ID even when its type or amount is later rejected.
  • D means deposit and W means withdrawal; letter case is normalized. Invalid records count as attempts. The first failure in the program's validation order is reported, and rejected records never change the balance.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter opening balance, number of attempts, then ID|D/W|amount for each attempt. Example: T1|W|1000.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

For every attempt: ID, acceptance or rejection reason, and unchanged or updated balance. The summary shows counts, deposit and withdrawal totals, and an arithmetic reconciliation.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read a valid opening balance and transaction attempt count.
  2. Initialize balance, deposit and withdrawal totals, counters, seen IDs, and audit results.
  3. Read a transaction. Check its shape, ID syntax, and whether that ID has already appeared.
  4. Reserve a new valid ID, then validate type and positive integer amount.
  5. For withdrawals, check denomination, per-transaction limit, daily limit, and remaining balance in that order.
  6. If valid, update balance and the relevant total. Otherwise record a rejection without altering money.
  7. Append the ID, status, and resulting balance to the audit list.
  8. After all attempts, print the audit and verify opening + deposits - withdrawals = final balance.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ opening_balance >= 500 and attempt_count in 1..50
balance <- opening_balance
seen_ids <- empty list; results <- empty list
deposited <- 0; withdrawn <- 0
accepted <- 0; rejected <- 0
FOR EACH attempt
    READ ID, type, amount
    reason <- empty
    VALIDATE record shape, ID syntax, and uniqueness
    IF new valid ID: ADD ID to seen_ids
    VALIDATE type in {D, W} and positive whole amount
    IF type = W AND no earlier error
        CHECK amount MOD 100 = 0
        CHECK amount <= 10000
        CHECK withdrawn + amount <= 20000
        CHECK balance - amount >= 500
    IF no error
        IF type = D
            balance <- balance + amount
            deposited <- deposited + amount
        ELSE
            balance <- balance - amount
            withdrawn <- withdrawn + amount
        accepted <- accepted + 1
    ELSE
        rejected <- rejected + 1
    APPEND (ID, status or first error, balance) to results
PRINT results, counts, and totals
PRINT opening_balance + deposited - withdrawn = balance
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 13_atm_transactions/program.py
Read the complete program 78 lines · no imports
print("ATM TRANSACTION SEQUENCE SIMULATION")
print("Use fictional transaction data. Amounts are whole rupees.")

opening_text = input("Opening balance (at least Rs 500): ").strip()
while not opening_text.isascii() or not opening_text.isdigit() or int(opening_text) < 500:
    print("ERROR: opening balance must be a whole number of at least 500.")
    opening_text = input("Opening balance (at least Rs 500): ").strip()
balance = int(opening_text)
opening_balance = balance

count_text = input("Number of transaction attempts (1-50): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 50:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 50.")
    count_text = input("Number of transaction attempts (1-50): ").strip()
transaction_count = int(count_text)

seen_ids = []
results = []
deposited = 0
withdrawn = 0
accepted = 0
rejected = 0
print("Transaction format: ID|D/W|amount")

for attempt in range(1, transaction_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Transaction {attempt}: ").split("|")
    transaction_id = f"row-{attempt}"
    reason = ""
    transaction_type = ""
    amount = 0
    if len(fields) != 3:
        reason = "expected ID|D/W|amount"
    else:
        transaction_id, transaction_type, amount_text = fields
        transaction_id = transaction_id.strip().upper()
        transaction_type = transaction_type.strip().upper()
        amount_text = amount_text.strip()
        if not 1 <= len(transaction_id) <= 12 or not transaction_id.isascii() or not transaction_id.isalnum():
            reason = "ID must contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits"
        elif transaction_id in seen_ids:
            reason = "duplicate transaction ID"
        else:
            seen_ids.append(transaction_id)
            if transaction_type not in ("D", "W"):
                reason = "transaction type must be D or W"
            elif not amount_text.isascii() or not amount_text.isdigit() or int(amount_text) == 0:
                reason = "amount must be a positive whole number"
            else:
                amount = int(amount_text)
                if transaction_type == "W":
                    if amount % 100 != 0:
                        reason = "withdrawal must be a multiple of Rs 100"
                    elif amount > 10000:
                        reason = "per-transaction withdrawal limit is Rs 10000"
                    elif withdrawn + amount > 20000:
                        reason = "daily withdrawal limit is Rs 20000"
                    elif balance - amount < 500:
                        reason = "withdrawal would breach the Rs 500 minimum balance"
    if reason == "":
        if transaction_type == "D":
            balance += amount
            deposited += amount
        else:
            balance -= amount
            withdrawn += amount
        accepted += 1
        results.append((transaction_id, f"ACCEPTED {transaction_type} Rs {amount}", balance))
    else:
        rejected += 1
        results.append((transaction_id, f"REJECTED: {reason}", balance))

print("\nTRANSACTION AUDIT")
for transaction_id, status, ending_balance in results:
    print(f"{transaction_id}: {status} | Balance Rs {ending_balance}")
print(f"Accepted: {accepted} | Rejected: {rejected}")
print(f"Deposits: Rs {deposited} | Withdrawals: Rs {withdrawn}")
print(f"Final balance: Rs {balance}")
print(f"Reconciliation: {opening_balance} + {deposited} - {withdrawn} = {balance}")

STUDY 03 / 10 BRIEF CASE 14

Warehouse Inventory Reconciliation

Lists · arithmetic · discrepancy flags6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Compare opening stock, receipts, dispatches, and physically observed closing stock for multiple products. Identify shortages and surpluses, reject impossible stock movement, and calculate each product's replenishment quantity against its target.

02 Objectives

  • Reconcile theoretical and physical stock using a stock-balance equation.
  • Distinguish invalid movement from an auditable physical discrepancy.
  • Calculate replenishment from the observed stock level.
  • Store and unpack multi-field product tuples and summarize audit counts.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: check record validity, calculate expected stock, compare, and replenish.
  • Pattern recognition: each product follows the same inventory-balance equation.
  • Abstraction: physical and book quantities are separate fields; neither overwrites the other.
  • Algorithm design: exclude invalid records before calculating the accepted-record summary.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • Accept 1-20 attempted product records. All quantities are nonnegative whole units of the same product; cross-product replenishment totals count units only.
  • Product codes contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits and normalize to uppercase. The first correctly shaped record with a valid code reserves that code, even if later numeric validation fails.
  • Expected closing stock = opening + incoming - dispatched. Dispatch greater than opening + incoming is impossible under this model and is rejected.
  • Difference = observed closing - expected closing. A negative difference is a shortage; a positive one is a surplus.
  • Observed stock may differ from the records and remains auditable even if it exceeds expected stock. Replenishment is target - observed when observed is below target, otherwise zero.
  • Invalid records count as attempts and contribute to neither stock calculations nor replenishment totals.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter the record count, then code|opening|incoming|dispatched|observed_closing|target. Example: P100|50|20|40|28|40.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Rejected-record reasons, expected and observed quantities, signed discrepancies, status, per-product replenishment, and audit totals.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read a valid record count and initialize products, seen codes, and rejection count.
  2. Read six fields per attempted record and validate the product code and uniqueness.
  3. Validate five nonnegative integer quantities.
  4. Reject dispatch above available stock; otherwise store the product tuple.
  5. For each stored tuple, calculate expected stock and observed - expected.
  6. Classify each difference as shortage, surplus, or match.
  7. Calculate replenishment from observed stock and add it to the total.
  8. Print the itemized audit, discrepancy count, rejected count, and replenishment total.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ record_count in 1..20
products <- empty list; seen_codes <- empty list
FOR EACH attempted record
    READ code, opening, incoming, dispatched, observed, target
    VALIDATE six fields and a new valid normalized code
    RESERVE each new syntactically valid code
    VALIDATE all quantities as nonnegative integers
    IF dispatched > opening + incoming: REJECT
    IF valid: APPEND the six-field product tuple
    ELSE: PRINT reason and increment rejected count
discrepancies <- 0; total_replenishment <- 0
FOR EACH product tuple
    expected <- opening + incoming - dispatched
    difference <- observed - expected
    IF difference < 0: status <- SHORTAGE
    ELSE IF difference > 0: status <- SURPLUS
    ELSE: status <- MATCH
    IF difference != 0: discrepancies <- discrepancies + 1
    replenish <- 0
    IF observed < target: replenish <- target - observed
    total_replenishment <- total_replenishment + replenish
    PRINT code, expected, observed, difference, status, replenish
PRINT audit and replenishment totals
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 14_warehouse_reconciliation/program.py
Read the complete program 65 lines · no imports
print("WAREHOUSE INVENTORY RECONCILIATION")
count_text = input("Number of product records (1-20): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 20:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 20.")
    count_text = input("Number of product records (1-20): ").strip()
record_count = int(count_text)
print("Format: code|opening|incoming|dispatched|observed_closing|target")

products = []
seen_codes = []
invalid_records = 0
for record_number in range(1, record_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Product {record_number}: ").split("|")
    reason = ""
    code = f"row-{record_number}"
    numbers = []
    if len(fields) != 6:
        reason = "expected six fields"
    else:
        code = fields[0].strip().upper()
        if not 1 <= len(code) <= 12 or not code.isascii() or not code.isalnum():
            reason = "code must contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits"
        elif code in seen_codes:
            reason = "duplicate product code"
        else:
            seen_codes.append(code)
            for field in fields[1:]:
                number_text = field.strip()
                if not number_text.isascii() or not number_text.isdigit():
                    reason = "quantities must be nonnegative whole numbers"
                else:
                    numbers.append(int(number_text))
            if reason == "":
                opening, incoming, dispatched, observed, target = numbers
                if dispatched > opening + incoming:
                    reason = "dispatch exceeds available stock"
                else:
                    products.append((code, opening, incoming, dispatched, observed, target))
    if reason != "":
        invalid_records += 1
        print(f"REJECTED {code}: {reason}")

print("\nSTOCK AUDIT")
print("Code | Expected | Observed | Difference | Status | Replenish")
discrepancies = 0
total_replenishment = 0
for code, opening, incoming, dispatched, observed, target in products:
    expected = opening + incoming - dispatched
    difference = observed - expected
    if difference < 0:
        status = "SHORTAGE"
        discrepancies += 1
    elif difference > 0:
        status = "SURPLUS"
        discrepancies += 1
    else:
        status = "MATCH"
    replenish = 0
    if observed < target:
        replenish = target - observed
    total_replenishment += replenish
    print(f"{code} | {expected} | {observed} | {difference:+d} | {status} | {replenish}")
print(f"Audited: {len(products)} | Rejected: {invalid_records}")
print(f"Products with discrepancies: {discrepancies}")
print(f"Total replenishment: {total_replenishment} units")

STUDY 04 / 10 BRIEF CASE 16

Multi-Day Water Tank Simulation

Simulation · loops · conservation6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Simulate a tank across a sequence of intervals with changing inflow and demand. Keep the stored level within capacity, measure overflow and unmet demand, identify the first interval in which a threshold is reached, and verify the water balance.

02 Objectives

  • Update a bounded state across multiple time intervals.
  • Distinguish demand, delivered water, spilled water, and shortage.
  • Detect threshold crossings before an interval's later withdrawal.
  • Check conservation using initial water, inflow, final water, supply, and spill.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: fill, spill, test the threshold, supply demand, and summarize.
  • Pattern recognition: the same state transition repeats each interval.
  • Abstraction: represent water as a scalar level and retain an interval tuple for the audit.
  • Algorithm design: enforce operation order so overflow and shortage can both occur in one interval.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • All values are whole litres. Capacity is positive; initial level and threshold lie between zero and capacity, inclusive. Accept 1-30 valid intervals.
  • Within each interval, all inflow occurs first, excess immediately spills, and demand is then supplied from the remaining stored water. There is no simultaneous-flow model.
  • Delivered water is the smaller of demand and stored water after filling. Unmet demand is demand minus delivered water.
  • The threshold means a stored level greater than or equal to the target. Check the initial level and the level after filling, before demand. A later fall below the threshold does not erase the first crossing.
  • Interval 0 denotes an initially met threshold. A zero threshold is therefore reached initially.
  • Malformed inflow/demand records are retried and do not advance time. There are no unrecorded leaks or evaporation.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter capacity, initial level, threshold, interval count, then inflow|demand for each interval. Example: 60|40.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

A table of start level, inflow, demand, delivered quantity, spill, shortage, and end level; aggregate flows; first threshold interval; and a conservation equation.

04 Algorithm

  1. Validate capacity, initial water, threshold, and interval count.
  2. Set the current level to initial water and record interval 0 if the threshold is already met.
  3. Read and validate inflow and demand, retrying malformed records.
  4. Save the starting level, add inflow, calculate any spill, and cap the stored level at capacity.
  5. If no earlier crossing exists and the filled level meets the threshold, record the current interval.
  6. Deliver demand up to the available level, calculate shortage, and subtract delivered water.
  7. Accumulate totals and append the interval audit tuple.
  8. After all intervals, print the audit and confirm initial + inflow = final + delivered + spill.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ valid capacity, initial, threshold, interval_count
level <- initial; first_crossing <- NOT_REACHED
IF initial >= threshold: first_crossing <- 0
INITIALIZE totals and interval records
WHILE completed intervals < interval_count
    READ inflow and demand
    IF either is not a nonnegative integer: PRINT error; RETRY
    start_level <- level
    level <- level + inflow
    spill <- 0
    IF level > capacity
        spill <- level - capacity
        level <- capacity
    IF first_crossing is NOT_REACHED AND level >= threshold
        first_crossing <- current interval number
    served <- demand; shortage <- 0
    IF demand > level
        served <- level
        shortage <- demand - level
    level <- level - served
    UPDATE flow totals
    APPEND (start, inflow, demand, served, spill, shortage, level)
PRINT interval audit and totals
PRINT initial crossing, first interval, or never
PRINT initial + total_inflow = level + total_served + total_spill
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 16_water_tank/program.py
Read the complete program 84 lines · no imports
print("MULTI-DAY WATER TANK SIMULATION")
capacity_text = input("Capacity in litres (positive integer): ").strip()
while not capacity_text.isascii() or not capacity_text.isdigit() or int(capacity_text) == 0:
    print("ERROR: capacity must be a positive whole number.")
    capacity_text = input("Capacity in litres (positive integer): ").strip()
capacity = int(capacity_text)

initial_text = input(f"Initial level (0-{capacity}): ").strip()
while not initial_text.isascii() or not initial_text.isdigit() or not 0 <= int(initial_text) <= capacity:
    print("ERROR: initial level must be within tank capacity.")
    initial_text = input(f"Initial level (0-{capacity}): ").strip()
initial = int(initial_text)
level = initial

threshold_text = input(f"Threshold (0-{capacity}): ").strip()
while not threshold_text.isascii() or not threshold_text.isdigit() or not 0 <= int(threshold_text) <= capacity:
    print("ERROR: threshold must be within tank capacity.")
    threshold_text = input(f"Threshold (0-{capacity}): ").strip()
threshold = int(threshold_text)

count_text = input("Number of intervals (1-30): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 30:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 30.")
    count_text = input("Number of intervals (1-30): ").strip()
interval_count = int(count_text)

records = []
total_inflow = 0
total_served = 0
total_spill = 0
total_shortage = 0
first_threshold_interval = -1
if level >= threshold:
    first_threshold_interval = 0
print("Each interval fills first, spills excess, then supplies demand.")
print("Format: inflow|demand")

while len(records) < interval_count:
    fields = input(f"Interval {len(records) + 1}: ").split("|")
    valid = len(fields) == 2
    if valid:
        for field in fields:
            number_text = field.strip()
            if not number_text.isascii() or not number_text.isdigit():
                valid = False
    if not valid:
        print("ERROR: enter two nonnegative whole numbers: inflow|demand.")
        continue
    inflow = int(fields[0].strip())
    demand = int(fields[1].strip())
    starting_level = level
    level += inflow
    spill = 0
    if level > capacity:
        spill = level - capacity
        level = capacity
    if first_threshold_interval == -1 and level >= threshold:
        first_threshold_interval = len(records) + 1
    served = demand
    shortage = 0
    if demand > level:
        served = level
        shortage = demand - level
    level -= served
    total_inflow += inflow
    total_served += served
    total_spill += spill
    total_shortage += shortage
    records.append((starting_level, inflow, demand, served, spill, shortage, level))

print("\nINTERVAL AUDIT (litres)")
print("Interval | Start | Inflow | Demand | Served | Spill | Shortage | End")
for record_index in range(len(records)):
    starting_level, inflow, demand, served, spill, shortage, ending_level = records[record_index]
    print(f"{record_index + 1} | {starting_level} | {inflow} | {demand} | {served} | {spill} | {shortage} | {ending_level}")
print(f"Final level: {level} litres")
print(f"Inflow: {total_inflow} | Served: {total_served} | Spill: {total_spill} | Shortage: {total_shortage}")
if first_threshold_interval == 0:
    print("Threshold first reached: initially (interval 0)")
elif first_threshold_interval == -1:
    print("Threshold first reached: never")
else:
    print(f"Threshold first reached: interval {first_threshold_interval}, after inflow")
print(f"Water balance: {initial} + {total_inflow} = {level} + {total_served} + {total_spill}")

STUDY 05 / 10 BRIEF CASE 23

Student Timetable Conflict Detection

Strings · tuples · interval overlap6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Validate a proposed timetable for one student. Parse course sessions from strings into tuples, detect overlapping sessions and simultaneous room bookings, identify sessions scheduled during room closures, and report whether the timetable is valid.

02 Objectives

  • Parse and validate strict 24-hour time strings using basic string operations.
  • Represent sessions and room closures as tuples with minute-based time intervals.
  • Use nested loops to compare unique session pairs.
  • Distinguish student conflicts, room conflicts, malformed records, and blocked bookings.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: parse sessions, check closures, compare pairs, and combine findings.
  • Pattern recognition: the same strict overlap test applies to sessions and closures.
  • Abstraction: replace clock strings with minutes after midnight.
  • Algorithm design: compare index pairs with the second index greater than the first to avoid double-counting.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • Accept 1-20 attempted session records for one student's timetable. Valid days are MON-FRI and valid rooms are R101, R102, and LAB2.
  • Assumed closures: LAB2 on WED from 10:00 to 12:00, and R102 on FRI from 13:00 to 14:00.
  • Course codes contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits. Course, day, and room text normalize to uppercase.
  • Times use exactly HH:MM, from 00:00 through 23:59. Each session ends after it starts on the same day. Overnight sessions and 24:00 are outside this model.
  • Intervals are half-open: [start, end). A session may end exactly when another begins or a closure starts. Overlap requires a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end.
  • Every same-day overlapping pair is a student conflict; it is additionally a room conflict if both rooms match. Compare each pair once.
  • Identical session tuples are rejected. A course may have distinct sessions. Syntactically valid sessions during closures remain in the pairwise audit so every problem is reported.
  • Any rejected record, student conflict, or blocked booking makes the complete timetable invalid.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter the number of attempts and then course|day|HH:MM|HH:MM|room. Example: CS101|MON|09:00|10:00|R101.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Rejected-record reasons, unavailable-room bookings, named conflict pairs, separate conflict counts, and a final VALID or INVALID verdict.

04 Algorithm

  1. Define valid days, rooms, and the supplied classroom closure tuples.
  2. Read a valid session count and validate each five-field record.
  3. Convert both valid HH:MM strings into hour * 60 + minute; require start < end.
  4. Reject duplicate session tuples; store other valid tuples.
  5. Compare each stored session with every closure for its room and day, reporting overlaps.
  6. Compare each unique pair of stored sessions on the same day using the strict overlap inequalities.
  7. Count every overlapping pair as a student conflict and, when rooms match, as a room conflict.
  8. Print counts and declare the timetable valid only when no rejection, overlap, or blocked booking exists.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
DEFINE valid days, rooms, and closure tuples
READ session_count in 1..20
sessions <- empty list; rejected <- 0
FOR EACH attempted record
    READ course, day, start_text, end_text, room
    VALIDATE fields, course code, day, and room
    FOR EACH of the two time strings
        CHECK exactly HH:MM, ASCII digits, hour 0..23, minute 0..59
        CONVERT to hour * 60 + minute
    CHECK start < end and tuple not already in sessions
    IF valid: APPEND (course, day, start, end, room)
    ELSE: PRINT reason; increment rejected
FOR EACH session AND EACH room closure
    IF same room and day AND start < closure_end AND end > closure_start
        REPORT unavailable booking
FOR first_index FROM 0 TO number_of_sessions - 1
    FOR second_index FROM first_index + 1 TO number_of_sessions - 1
        IF same day AND first_start < second_end AND second_start < first_end
            REPORT student conflict
            IF rooms match: ALSO COUNT room conflict
PRINT counts
IF no rejected records, student conflicts, or blocked bookings
    PRINT VALID
ELSE: PRINT INVALID
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 23_timetable_conflicts/program.py
Read the complete program 89 lines · no imports
print("STUDENT TIMETABLE CONFLICT DETECTION")
days = ("MON", "TUE", "WED", "THU", "FRI")
rooms = ("R101", "R102", "LAB2")
unavailable = [("LAB2", "WED", 600, 720), ("R102", "FRI", 780, 840)]
print("Rooms: R101, R102, LAB2. Days: MON-FRI.")
print("Unavailable: LAB2 WED 10:00-12:00; R102 FRI 13:00-14:00.")
print("Format: course|day|HH:MM|HH:MM|room")

count_text = input("Number of session records (1-20): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 20:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 20.")
    count_text = input("Number of session records (1-20): ").strip()
session_count = int(count_text)
sessions = []
rejected = 0

for record_number in range(1, session_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Session {record_number}: ").split("|")
    reason = ""
    if len(fields) != 5:
        reason = "expected five fields"
    else:
        course, day, start_text, end_text, room = fields
        course = course.strip().upper()
        day = day.strip().upper()
        room = room.strip().upper()
        times = []
        if not 1 <= len(course) <= 12 or not course.isascii() or not course.isalnum():
            reason = "course must contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits"
        elif day not in days or room not in rooms:
            reason = "unknown day or room"
        else:
            for time_text in (start_text.strip(), end_text.strip()):
                valid_time = len(time_text) == 5 and time_text[2] == ":"
                if valid_time:
                    hour_text = time_text[:2]
                    minute_text = time_text[3:]
                    valid_time = hour_text.isascii() and hour_text.isdigit() and minute_text.isascii() and minute_text.isdigit()
                    if valid_time:
                        hour = int(hour_text)
                        minute = int(minute_text)
                        valid_time = 0 <= hour <= 23 and 0 <= minute <= 59
                if valid_time:
                    times.append(hour * 60 + minute)
                else:
                    reason = "times must use valid 24-hour HH:MM format"
            if reason == "":
                start, end = times
                session = (course, day, start, end, room)
                if start >= end:
                    reason = "end time must be later than start time on the same day"
                elif session in sessions:
                    reason = "duplicate session"
                else:
                    sessions.append(session)
    if reason != "":
        rejected += 1
        print(f"REJECTED row {record_number}: {reason}")

print("\nTIMETABLE AUDIT")
blocked_bookings = 0
student_conflicts = 0
room_conflicts = 0
for course, day, start, end, room in sessions:
    for blocked_room, blocked_day, blocked_start, blocked_end in unavailable:
        if room == blocked_room and day == blocked_day and start < blocked_end and end > blocked_start:
            blocked_bookings += 1
            print(f"UNAVAILABLE: {course} in {room} on {day}")

for first_index in range(len(sessions)):
    first_course, first_day, first_start, first_end, first_room = sessions[first_index]
    for second_index in range(first_index + 1, len(sessions)):
        second_course, second_day, second_start, second_end, second_room = sessions[second_index]
        if first_day == second_day and first_start < second_end and second_start < first_end:
            student_conflicts += 1
            detail = "student"
            if first_room == second_room:
                room_conflicts += 1
                detail += f"; room {first_room}"
            print(f"CONFLICT: {first_course} / {second_course} ({first_day}): {detail}")

print(f"Parsed sessions: {len(sessions)} | Rejected records: {rejected}")
print(f"Student conflict pairs: {student_conflicts}")
print(f"Room conflict pairs: {room_conflicts}")
print(f"Unavailable-room bookings: {blocked_bookings}")
if rejected == 0 and student_conflicts == 0 and blocked_bookings == 0:
    print("Timetable: VALID")
else:
    print("Timetable: INVALID")

STUDY 06 / 10 BRIEF CASE 27

Advanced Numeric Pattern Generator

Nested loops · symmetry · alignment6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Generate a hollow, symmetric numeric diamond for a user-specified number of levels. Validate the dimension, preserve alignment, and handle the single-level boundary without printing a duplicate digit.

02 Objectives

  • Use nested loops to map rows and columns to a pattern.
  • Derive the matching upper and lower halves from one level formula.
  • Print only boundary digits while preserving the hollow interior.
  • Validate dimensions and report the generated height, width, and digit count.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate the size, determine each row's level, determine boundaries, and print.
  • Pattern recognition: lower-half levels mirror the upper half.
  • Abstraction: a cell needs only its row, column, and the two edge positions.
  • Algorithm design: one nested row/column loop handles both halves and the size-one case.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • The chosen variant of the brief is a hollow numeric diamond. A level is represented by its own digit.
  • Accept an integer size from 1 to 9 so every printed value occupies one character.
  • The output has 2 * size - 1 rows and the same maximum width. Spaces between the two edge digits remain blank.
  • Rows are shown in a monospaced font. Leading spaces are meaningful; trailing spaces are removed.
  • Invalid sizes are retried. At size 1, the left and right edges coincide and print one digit.

INPUT CONTRACT

One integer size in 1-9. Example: 4.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

A hollow numeric diamond followed by its height, maximum width, and the number of printed digits.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read and validate size between 1 and 9.
  2. Set dimension = 2 * size - 1 and digit count = 0.
  3. For each row from 1 through dimension, use level = row in the upper half and level = 2 * size - row in the lower half.
  4. Calculate left_edge = size - level + 1 and right_edge = size + level - 1.
  5. Scan all columns. Append the level digit when the column matches either edge; otherwise append one space.
  6. Increment the digit count only once for each printed cell, including coincident edges.
  7. Remove trailing spaces and print the completed row.
  8. Print the height, maximum width, and digit count.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ valid size in 1..9
dimension <- 2 * size - 1
digit_count <- 0
FOR row FROM 1 TO dimension
    IF row <= size: level <- row
    ELSE: level <- 2 * size - row
    left_edge <- size - level + 1
    right_edge <- size + level - 1
    line <- empty string
    FOR column FROM 1 TO dimension
        IF column = left_edge OR column = right_edge
            APPEND text(level) to line
            digit_count <- digit_count + 1
        ELSE
            APPEND one space to line
    REMOVE trailing spaces from line
    PRINT line
PRINT dimension as height and maximum width
PRINT digit_count
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 27_numeric_diamond/program.py
Read the complete program 27 lines · no imports
print("HOLLOW NUMERIC DIAMOND")
size_text = input("Number of levels (1-9): ").strip()
while not size_text.isascii() or not size_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(size_text) <= 9:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 9.")
    size_text = input("Number of levels (1-9): ").strip()
size = int(size_text)
dimension = 2 * size - 1
digit_count = 0
print("\nPATTERN")

for row_number in range(1, dimension + 1):
    level = row_number
    if row_number > size:
        level = 2 * size - row_number
    left_edge = size - level + 1
    right_edge = size + level - 1
    line = ""
    for column_number in range(1, dimension + 1):
        if column_number == left_edge or column_number == right_edge:
            line += str(level)
            digit_count += 1
        else:
            line += " "
    print(line.rstrip())

print(f"Height: {dimension} | Maximum width: {dimension}")
print(f"Digits printed: {digit_count}")

STUDY 07 / 10 BRIEF CASE 29

Password Policy Validation Engine

Character scanning · strings · reasons6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Evaluate fictional password samples against a declared length, character-category, repetition, and prohibited-substring policy. Report every failed condition for each sample, without repeating the full password in the result audit.

02 Objectives

  • Scan strings using loops and character comparisons.
  • Collect every policy failure instead of stopping after the first one.
  • Detect consecutive character runs and case-insensitive substrings.
  • Separate input-format errors from password-policy failures.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate record shape, scan categories, detect runs, and inspect substrings.
  • Pattern recognition: one scan can collect category flags and run lengths together.
  • Abstraction: represent compliance through booleans and a list of failure explanations.
  • Algorithm design: accept only when the full failure list remains empty.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • This is a string-processing classroom policy, not a production authentication system. Use fictional sample strings. Normal input() entry is visible in a terminal; only the audit avoids printing full passwords.
  • Accept 1-20 samples in username|password form, with exactly one separator. Usernames contain 3-20 ASCII letters or digits.
  • Password length is 10-64 characters. Require at least one ASCII uppercase letter, lowercase letter, digit, and one special character from !@#$%^&*?_-.
  • Only those character groups are allowed. Password whitespace is preserved and rejected; it is not silently stripped. The pipe character is not an allowed password character.
  • Three or more identical consecutive characters are prohibited. Repetition matching is case-sensitive.
  • The substrings password, admin, qwerty, and 1234 are forbidden regardless of case. A valid username must not appear in the password regardless of case.
  • Malformed records are rejected as samples. For a correctly shaped record, report all independently testable failures. An invalid username does not prevent evaluation of the other password rules.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter the sample count, then username|password. Example fictional input: Mira|M8!riverOak.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Sample number and username, ACCEPTED or REJECTED status, every failed condition, and accepted/rejected totals.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read a valid sample count and initialize result and summary lists/counters.
  2. Split each sample on the separator; reject malformed records.
  3. Check username syntax and password length.
  4. Scan every password character to set category flags, flag disallowed characters, and detect runs of at least three identical characters.
  5. Append a separate failure for each missing category, invalid-character condition, and prohibited run.
  6. Compare a lowercase copy with every prohibited substring and the valid username.
  7. Store the sample number, username, and complete failure list.
  8. Print ACCEPTED for empty failure lists; otherwise print REJECTED and all reasons. Print totals.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ sample_count in 1..20
DEFINE allowed special characters and prohibited substrings
FOR EACH sample
    failures <- empty list
    READ username|password without trimming password
    IF record does not contain exactly two fields
        ADD malformed-record failure
    ELSE
        CHECK username syntax and password length
        INITIALIZE category flags, run length, and previous character
        FOR EACH character IN password
            SET its ASCII category flag OR flag invalid character
            IF character = previous: increment run length
            ELSE: run length <- 1
            IF run length >= 3: flag prohibited repetition
            previous <- character
        ADD a failure for every missing category
        ADD invalid-character and repetition failures when applicable
        FOR EACH prohibited substring
            IF it appears in lowercase(password): ADD its failure
        IF username is valid AND lowercase(username) appears in lowercase(password)
            ADD username-substring failure
    STORE (sample number, username, failures)
    UPDATE accepted or rejected count
PRINT every sample status and every failure
PRINT totals
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 29_password_validation/program.py
Read the complete program 88 lines · no imports
print("PASSWORD POLICY VALIDATION ENGINE")
print("Enter fictional samples only: username|password")
print("Passwords are not echoed in the audit.")
count_text = input("Number of samples (1-20): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 20:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 20.")
    count_text = input("Number of samples (1-20): ").strip()
sample_count = int(count_text)

special_characters = "!@#$%^&*?_-"
prohibited = ("password", "admin", "qwerty", "1234")
accepted = 0
rejected = 0
results = []

for sample_number in range(1, sample_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Sample {sample_number}: ").split("|")
    failures = []
    username = "(malformed)"
    if len(fields) != 2:
        failures.append("Expected username|password with exactly one separator.")
    else:
        username = fields[0].strip()
        password = fields[1]
        username_valid = 3 <= len(username) <= 20 and username.isascii() and username.isalnum()
        if not username_valid:
            failures.append("Username must contain 3-20 ASCII letters or digits.")
        if not 10 <= len(password) <= 64:
            failures.append("Password length must be 10-64 characters.")
        has_upper = False
        has_lower = False
        has_digit = False
        has_special = False
        invalid_characters = False
        repeated_run = False
        previous_character = ""
        run_length = 0
        for character in password:
            if "A" <= character <= "Z":
                has_upper = True
            elif "a" <= character <= "z":
                has_lower = True
            elif "0" <= character <= "9":
                has_digit = True
            elif character in special_characters:
                has_special = True
            else:
                invalid_characters = True
            if character == previous_character:
                run_length += 1
            else:
                run_length = 1
            if run_length >= 3:
                repeated_run = True
            previous_character = character
        if not has_upper:
            failures.append("Include an uppercase ASCII letter.")
        if not has_lower:
            failures.append("Include a lowercase ASCII letter.")
        if not has_digit:
            failures.append("Include an ASCII digit.")
        if not has_special:
            failures.append("Include a special character from !@#$%^&*?_-")
        if invalid_characters:
            failures.append("Only ASCII letters, digits, and the listed special characters are allowed.")
        if repeated_run:
            failures.append("Three or more consecutive identical characters are prohibited.")
        lowered_password = password.lower()
        for forbidden_text in prohibited:
            if forbidden_text in lowered_password:
                failures.append(f"Prohibited substring: {forbidden_text}")
        if username_valid and username.lower() in lowered_password:
            failures.append("Password must not contain the username (case-insensitive).")
    if len(failures) == 0:
        accepted += 1
    else:
        rejected += 1
    results.append((sample_number, username, failures))

print("\nPOLICY AUDIT")
for sample_number, username, failures in results:
    if len(failures) == 0:
        print(f"Sample {sample_number} ({username}): ACCEPTED")
    else:
        print(f"Sample {sample_number} ({username}): REJECTED")
        for failure in failures:
            print(f"  - {failure}")
print(f"Accepted: {accepted} | Rejected: {rejected}")

STUDY 08 / 10 BRIEF CASE 31

String-Based Examination Answer Evaluation

Indexing · negative marking · ties6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Compare student answer strings with an answer key. Count correct, incorrect, and unanswered responses, apply positive and negative marking, classify results using stated thresholds, and identify all students tied for the top valid score.

02 Objectives

  • Validate answer strings before accessing matching character positions.
  • Use string indexing to count three mutually exclusive response outcomes.
  • Apply negative marking without silently clamping negative totals.
  • Handle top-score ties and the case where no valid student record exists.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate the key, validate each record, score positions, and rank.
  • Pattern recognition: each character position produces exactly one response outcome.
  • Abstraction: an answer string is an ordered list of symbols, not free-form text.
  • Algorithm design: initialize the maximum below the lowest possible score so all-negative results still rank correctly.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • The answer key contains 1-50 letters A-D; letter case is normalized. Accept 1-30 attempted student records.
  • Student IDs contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits and normalize to uppercase. A correctly shaped row with a valid new ID reserves the ID even if its answer string is invalid.
  • Each response string has exactly the key length and contains A-D or '-' for unanswered. Outer whitespace is stripped; interior whitespace is invalid.
  • Correct = +4 marks, incorrect = -1, unanswered = 0. Final scores may be negative. Maximum score = 4 * question_count.
  • Percentage = score * 100 / maximum. At least 75% gives DISTINCTION, at least 50% gives PASS, otherwise NEEDS PRACTICE.
  • Malformed student records count as attempts and are excluded from scores and ranking. All top-score ties are shown in input order.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter the answer key, record count, and ID|responses for each student. Example: S02|AB-D for key ABCD.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Rejected-record reasons; correct, incorrect, and unanswered counts; score, percentage and classification; evaluation totals; and top-score ties.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read and validate a nonempty key containing only A-D, then a valid student record count.
  2. Validate each record's shape and unique ID, then its response length and permitted symbols.
  3. For every answer position, count '-' as unanswered, an equal symbol as correct, and any other permitted symbol as incorrect.
  4. Calculate score = 4 * correct - incorrect and percentage against the maximum.
  5. Assign the classification using the 75% and 50% boundaries.
  6. Store valid result tuples and print reasons for invalid records.
  7. Print valid results and track the highest score, retaining all ties.
  8. If none are valid, explicitly report that no top score is available.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ a valid answer_key of 1..50 symbols A-D
READ student_count in 1..30
seen_ids <- empty list; results <- empty list
FOR EACH attempted student record
    READ ID and responses; normalize letter case
    VALIDATE record, new ID, exact length, and symbols A-D or '-'
    RESERVE syntactically valid IDs in correctly shaped records
    IF invalid: PRINT reason and increment rejected
    ELSE
        correct <- 0; incorrect <- 0; unanswered <- 0
        FOR position FROM 0 TO key length - 1
            IF responses[position] = '-': increment unanswered
            ELSE IF responses[position] = key[position]: increment correct
            ELSE: increment incorrect
        score <- 4 * correct - incorrect
        percentage <- score * 100 / (4 * key length)
        IF percentage >= 75: classification <- DISTINCTION
        ELSE IF percentage >= 50: classification <- PASS
        ELSE: classification <- NEEDS PRACTICE
        APPEND result tuple
highest <- -(key length) - 1
FOR EACH result: PRINT result and UPDATE highest score and ties
PRINT evaluated and rejected counts
IF results is empty: PRINT no valid top score
ELSE: PRINT highest score and all tied IDs
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 31_answer_evaluation/program.py
Read the complete program 82 lines · no imports
print("STRING-BASED EXAMINATION ANSWER EVALUATION")
key_valid = False
while not key_valid:
    answer_key = input("Answer key (1-50 letters A-D): ").strip().upper()
    key_valid = 1 <= len(answer_key) <= 50
    for answer in answer_key:
        if answer not in "ABCD":
            key_valid = False
    if not key_valid:
        print("ERROR: the answer key must contain 1-50 letters A-D.")

count_text = input("Number of student records (1-30): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 30:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 30.")
    count_text = input("Number of student records (1-30): ").strip()
student_count = int(count_text)
print(f"Format: ID|{len(answer_key)} responses. Use - for unanswered.")
seen_ids = []
results = []
rejected = 0

for record_number in range(1, student_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Student {record_number}: ").split("|")
    reason = ""
    student_id = f"row-{record_number}"
    if len(fields) != 2:
        reason = "expected ID|responses"
    else:
        student_id = fields[0].strip().upper()
        responses = fields[1].strip().upper()
        if not 1 <= len(student_id) <= 12 or not student_id.isascii() or not student_id.isalnum():
            reason = "ID must contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits"
        elif student_id in seen_ids:
            reason = "duplicate student ID"
        else:
            seen_ids.append(student_id)
            if len(responses) != len(answer_key):
                reason = "response length must match the answer key"
            else:
                for answer in responses:
                    if answer not in "ABCD-":
                        reason = "responses must contain only A-D or -"
            if reason == "":
                correct = 0
                incorrect = 0
                unanswered = 0
                for answer_index in range(len(answer_key)):
                    if responses[answer_index] == "-":
                        unanswered += 1
                    elif responses[answer_index] == answer_key[answer_index]:
                        correct += 1
                    else:
                        incorrect += 1
                score = correct * 4 - incorrect
                percentage = score * 100 / (len(answer_key) * 4)
                if percentage >= 75:
                    classification = "DISTINCTION"
                elif percentage >= 50:
                    classification = "PASS"
                else:
                    classification = "NEEDS PRACTICE"
                results.append((student_id, correct, incorrect, unanswered, score, percentage, classification))
    if reason != "":
        rejected += 1
        print(f"REJECTED {student_id}: {reason}")

print("\nEXAMINATION RESULTS")
print("ID | Correct | Incorrect | Blank | Score | Percent | Result")
highest_score = -len(answer_key) - 1
top_students = []
for student_id, correct, incorrect, unanswered, score, percentage, classification in results:
    print(f"{student_id} | {correct} | {incorrect} | {unanswered} | {score} | {percentage:.2f}% | {classification}")
    if score > highest_score:
        highest_score = score
        top_students = [student_id]
    elif score == highest_score:
        top_students.append(student_id)
print(f"Evaluated: {len(results)} | Rejected: {rejected}")
if len(results) > 0:
    print(f"Top score: {highest_score}/{len(answer_key) * 4} ({', '.join(top_students)})")
else:
    print("Top score: no valid student records")

STUDY 09 / 10 BRIEF CASE 42

Student Marks Matrix Analysis

Nested lists · row/column statistics6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Analyze a matrix of student marks across subjects. Calculate student totals and averages, determine classifications using subject-wise passing requirements, calculate subject totals, averages and extrema, identify tied top performers, and flag subjects with low average performance.

02 Objectives

  • Represent marks as a validated rectangular nested list.
  • Traverse the matrix by rows for student statistics and by columns for subject statistics.
  • Keep subject-wise pass criteria separate from average-based classifications.
  • Report all top-score ties and subjects below a specified average.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate matrix dimensions, calculate rows, calculate columns, and summarize.
  • Pattern recognition: the same aggregation pattern applies to each row and each column.
  • Abstraction: keep student identifiers and subject labels separate from the numeric matrix.
  • Algorithm design: use nested index loops so each mark is attributed to its correct student and subject.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • Accept 1-20 students and 1-10 subjects. Marks are whole numbers from 0 to 100, inclusive.
  • Subject codes and student IDs contain 1-12 ASCII letters or digits, normalize to uppercase, and must be unique within their respective lists.
  • Invalid subject lists and student rows are retried. The matrix is not analyzed until every requested row is valid and complete.
  • A mark of at least 40 is required in every subject. Any lower mark makes the student FAIL regardless of average.
  • Among students passing every subject: average >= 75 gives DISTINCTION; average >= 60 gives FIRST CLASS; all remaining passing averages give PASS.
  • A subject is flagged when its class average is strictly below 50. Exactly 50 is not flagged.
  • Overall top performers are determined by total marks across all valid students, independent of pass classification. Subject toppers use that subject's mark. Every tie is retained in input order.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter student count, subject count, a pipe-separated subject-code list, then ID|mark1|...|markN for each student.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Student totals, averages, failed subjects and classifications; subject totals, averages, lowest/highest marks and toppers; overall top ties, overall average, and low-average subject labels.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read valid student and subject counts.
  2. Read a complete unique subject-code list; retry malformed lists.
  3. Read student rows, validating ID uniqueness, exact mark count, and the 0-100 range.
  4. Append each accepted ID and its marks list to parallel identifier and matrix lists.
  5. For each row, sum marks, identify failed subjects, calculate the average, and apply classification rules.
  6. Track the highest total and all tied student IDs while accumulating the grand total.
  7. For each column, calculate total, average, minimum, maximum, and all subject toppers.
  8. Flag averages below 50 and print the overall average, overall top ties, and weak subjects.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ student_count in 1..20 and subject_count in 1..10
READ exactly subject_count unique valid subject codes; RETRY errors
student_ids <- empty list; marks_matrix <- empty nested list
WHILE accepted students < student_count
    READ ID and subject_count marks
    CHECK new valid ID, correct row length, and integer marks 0..100
    IF invalid: PRINT error; RETRY
    ELSE: APPEND ID and the marks row
FOR EACH student row
    total <- 0; failed_subjects <- empty list
    FOR EACH subject column
        ADD mark to total
        IF mark < 40: APPEND subject label to failed_subjects
    average <- total / subject_count
    IF failed_subjects is not empty: classification <- FAIL
    ELSE IF average >= 75: classification <- DISTINCTION
    ELSE IF average >= 60: classification <- FIRST CLASS
    ELSE: classification <- PASS
    PRINT row statistics; UPDATE highest total and ties
    ADD total to grand_total
FOR EACH subject column
    SCAN all rows for total, minimum, maximum, and all maximum ties
    average <- total / student_count
    IF average < 50: APPEND subject to weak_subjects
    PRINT column statistics
PRINT overall top ties
PRINT grand_total / (student_count * subject_count)
PRINT weak_subjects or none
STOP

print("STUDENT MARKS MATRIX ANALYSIS")
student_count_text = input("Number of students (1-20): ").strip()
while not student_count_text.isascii() or not student_count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(student_count_text) <= 20:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 20.")
    student_count_text = input("Number of students (1-20): ").strip()
student_count = int(student_count_text)

subject_count_text = input("Number of subjects (1-10): ").strip()
while not subject_count_text.isascii() or not subject_count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(subject_count_text) <= 10:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 10.")
    subject_count_text = input("Number of subjects (1-10): ").strip()
subject_count = int(subject_count_text)

subjects = []
while len(subjects) != subject_count:
    fields = input(f"Enter {subject_count} unique subject codes separated by |: ").split("|")
    subjects = []
    valid_subjects = len(fields) == subject_count
    for field in fields:
        subject = field.strip().upper()
        if not 1 <= len(subject) <= 12 or not subject.isascii() or not subject.isalnum() or subject in subjects:
            valid_subjects = False
        subjects.append(subject)
    if not valid_subjects:
        print("ERROR: use the correct number of unique ASCII alphanumeric subject codes.")
        subjects = []

student_ids = []
marks_matrix = []
print("Format: ID|mark1|mark2|...; marks must be integers from 0 to 100.")
while len(student_ids) < student_count:
    fields = input(f"Student {len(student_ids) + 1}: ").split("|")
    if len(fields) != subject_count + 1:
        print("ERROR: provide one ID and exactly one mark per subject.")
        continue
    student_id = fields[0].strip().upper()
    if not 1 <= len(student_id) <= 12 or not student_id.isascii() or not student_id.isalnum() or student_id in student_ids:
        print("ERROR: student IDs must be unique ASCII alphanumeric strings of 1-12 characters.")
        continue
    marks = []
    valid_marks = True
    for field in fields[1:]:
        mark_text = field.strip()
        if not mark_text.isascii() or not mark_text.isdigit() or not 0 <= int(mark_text) <= 100:
            valid_marks = False
        else:
            marks.append(int(mark_text))
    if not valid_marks:
        print("ERROR: each mark must be a whole number from 0 to 100.")
        continue
    student_ids.append(student_id)
    marks_matrix.append(marks)

print("\nSTUDENT STATISTICS")
print("ID | Total | Average | Failed subjects | Classification")
highest_total = -1
top_students = []
grand_total = 0
for student_index in range(student_count):
    total = 0
    failed_subjects = []
    for subject_index in range(subject_count):
        mark = marks_matrix[student_index][subject_index]
        total += mark
        if mark < 40:
            failed_subjects.append(subjects[subject_index])
    average = total / subject_count
    if len(failed_subjects) > 0:
        classification = "FAIL"
    elif average >= 75:
        classification = "DISTINCTION"
    elif average >= 60:
        classification = "FIRST CLASS"
    else:
        classification = "PASS"
    failed_text = "none"
    if len(failed_subjects) > 0:
        failed_text = ", ".join(failed_subjects)
    print(f"{student_ids[student_index]} | {total} | {average:.2f} | {failed_text} | {classification}")
    grand_total += total
    if total > highest_total:
        highest_total = total
        top_students = [student_ids[student_index]]
    elif total == highest_total:
        top_students.append(student_ids[student_index])

print("\nSUBJECT STATISTICS")
print("Subject | Total | Average | Lowest | Highest | Top students")
weak_subjects = []
for subject_index in range(subject_count):
    total = 0
    lowest = 101
    highest = -1
    subject_toppers = []
    for student_index in range(student_count):
        mark = marks_matrix[student_index][subject_index]
        total += mark
        if mark < lowest:
            lowest = mark
        if mark > highest:
            highest = mark
            subject_toppers = [student_ids[student_index]]
        elif mark == highest:
            subject_toppers.append(student_ids[student_index])
    average = total / student_count
    if average < 50:
        weak_subjects.append(subjects[subject_index])
    print(f"{subjects[subject_index]} | {total} | {average:.2f} | {lowest} | {highest} | {', '.join(subject_toppers)}")

print(f"Top overall total: {highest_total}/{subject_count * 100} ({', '.join(top_students)})")
print(f"Overall average: {grand_total / (student_count * subject_count):.2f}")
if len(weak_subjects) == 0:
    print("Subjects averaging below 50: none")
else:
    print(f"Subjects averaging below 50: {', '.join(weak_subjects)}")

STUDY 10 / 10 BRIEF CASE 49

Tuple-Based Product Catalogue Audit

Tuple unpacking · money · audit6 / 6 TESTS PASSED

01 Problem statement

Store product identifiers, unit prices, stock, and reorder levels as tuples. Audit malformed and duplicate records, calculate product and total inventory values, and identify the items and quantities requiring replenishment.

02 Objectives

  • Validate structured product identifiers and decimal-price strings.
  • Convert prices into integer paise using only string and integer operations.
  • Store immutable product records in tuples and unpack them for analysis.
  • Exclude invalid records from inventory valuation and replenishment totals.

Computational thinking

  • Decomposition: validate identity, parse the price, validate quantities, and value inventory.
  • Pattern recognition: every valid tuple supports the same stock-times-price calculation.
  • Abstraction: use integer paise so decimal-input formatting does not control arithmetic accuracy.
  • Algorithm design: reject invalid records before appending typed tuples to the catalogue.

03 Assumptions & policy

  • Accept 1-30 attempted records. Product IDs normalize to uppercase and must be P followed by exactly three ASCII digits.
  • The first correctly shaped row with a syntactically valid new ID reserves that ID, even if a later price or stock check fails. Repeated IDs are rejected.
  • Prices are positive rupee amounts with a required integer part and optionally one or two decimal places: 12, 12.5, and 12.50 are valid; .50, 1., negatives, and excess precision are invalid.
  • Convert prices to integer paise. Inventory arithmetic stays in paise; rupee conversion is only for display.
  • Stock and reorder level are nonnegative whole units. A zero reorder level is permitted.
  • Replenishment is reorder_level - stock when stock is lower, otherwise zero. Stock equal to the reorder level does not trigger replenishment.
  • Invalid records count as attempts but contribute to neither inventory value nor replenishment. The report shows the first validation error for each rejected row.

INPUT CONTRACT

Enter the record count, then Pddd|price_in_Rs|stock|reorder_level. Example: P002|3.75|2|8.

PROGRAM OUTPUT

Rejected-record reasons; each valid product's unit price, stock, inventory value and replenishment; total value; total units needed; and item IDs below their reorder levels.

04 Algorithm

  1. Read a valid record count and initialize the catalogue, seen IDs, and rejection count.
  2. Validate four fields and the Pddd identifier; reject repeated IDs and reserve each new valid ID.
  3. Split the price around the decimal point, require a digit-only integer part and at most two fractional digits, and pad a single fractional digit with zero.
  4. Convert whole rupees and fractional paise to one positive integer price.
  5. Validate stock and reorder level as nonnegative integers, then append the typed product tuple.
  6. For each valid tuple, calculate value = unit_price_paise * stock.
  7. Calculate the replenishment gap, retain below-level product IDs, and accumulate value and unit totals.
  8. Print the catalogue audit, rejection count, total value, and replenishment summary.

05 Flowchart

06 Pseudocode

START
READ record_count in 1..30
catalogue <- empty list; seen_ids <- empty list
FOR EACH attempted record
    READ ID, price_text, stock_text, reorder_text
    CHECK four fields, Pddd ID format, and uniqueness
    RESERVE every new syntactically valid ID
    SPLIT price_text on decimal point
    REQUIRE one or two parts and an ASCII integer part
    IF a fraction is present: REQUIRE one or two ASCII digits
    PAD one fractional digit to two; absent fraction becomes 00
    price_paise <- integer_part * 100 + fractional_paise
    CHECK price_paise > 0 and nonnegative whole stock/reorder values
    IF valid: APPEND (ID, price_paise, stock, reorder_level)
    ELSE: PRINT reason; increment rejected
inventory_value <- 0; replenishment_units <- 0
FOR EACH (ID, price_paise, stock, reorder_level) IN catalogue
    value <- price_paise * stock
    replenish <- 0
    IF stock < reorder_level
        replenish <- reorder_level - stock
        RECORD ID for replenishment
    ACCUMULATE value and replenish
    PRINT product values formatted in rupees
PRINT valid/rejected counts, total value, units needed, and item IDs
STOP

07 Python source

RUN FROM REPOSITORY ROOTpython3 49_product_catalogue/program.py
Read the complete program 76 lines · no imports
print("TUPLE-BASED PRODUCT CATALOGUE AUDIT")
count_text = input("Number of catalogue records (1-30): ").strip()
while not count_text.isascii() or not count_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(count_text) <= 30:
    print("ERROR: enter an integer from 1 to 30.")
    count_text = input("Number of catalogue records (1-30): ").strip()
record_count = int(count_text)
print("Format: Pddd|price_in_Rs|stock|reorder_level")
print("Prices must be positive, with at most two decimal places.")

catalogue = []
seen_ids = []
rejected = 0
for record_number in range(1, record_count + 1):
    fields = input(f"Product {record_number}: ").split("|")
    reason = ""
    product_id = f"row-{record_number}"
    if len(fields) != 4:
        reason = "expected four fields"
    else:
        product_id, price_text, stock_text, reorder_text = fields
        product_id = product_id.strip().upper()
        price_text = price_text.strip()
        stock_text = stock_text.strip()
        reorder_text = reorder_text.strip()
        if len(product_id) != 4 or product_id[0] != "P" or not product_id[1:].isascii() or not product_id[1:].isdigit():
            reason = "ID must be P followed by three ASCII digits"
        elif product_id in seen_ids:
            reason = "duplicate product ID"
        else:
            seen_ids.append(product_id)
            price_parts = price_text.split(".")
            price_valid = len(price_parts) in (1, 2)
            if price_valid:
                whole = price_parts[0]
                fraction = "00"
                price_valid = whole.isascii() and whole.isdigit()
                if len(price_parts) == 2:
                    fraction = price_parts[1]
                    price_valid = price_valid and 1 <= len(fraction) <= 2 and fraction.isascii() and fraction.isdigit()
                    fraction = (fraction + "00")[:2]
            if not price_valid:
                reason = "invalid price format"
            else:
                price_paise = int(whole) * 100 + int(fraction)
                if price_paise == 0:
                    reason = "price must be positive"
                elif not stock_text.isascii() or not stock_text.isdigit() or not reorder_text.isascii() or not reorder_text.isdigit():
                    reason = "stock and reorder level must be nonnegative whole numbers"
                else:
                    catalogue.append((product_id, price_paise, int(stock_text), int(reorder_text)))
    if reason != "":
        rejected += 1
        print(f"REJECTED {product_id}: {reason}")

print("\nCATALOGUE AUDIT")
print("ID | Unit price (Rs) | Stock | Value (Rs) | Reorder level | Replenish")
inventory_value = 0
replenishment_units = 0
reorder_items = []
for product_id, price_paise, stock, reorder_level in catalogue:
    value = price_paise * stock
    inventory_value += value
    replenish = 0
    if stock < reorder_level:
        replenish = reorder_level - stock
        reorder_items.append(product_id)
    replenishment_units += replenish
    print(f"{product_id} | {price_paise / 100:.2f} | {stock} | {value / 100:.2f} | {reorder_level} | {replenish}")

print(f"Valid records: {len(catalogue)} | Rejected: {rejected}")
print(f"Inventory value: Rs {inventory_value / 100:.2f}")
print(f"Replenishment needed: {replenishment_units} units")
if len(reorder_items) == 0:
    print("Items below reorder level: none")
else:
    print(f"Items below reorder level: {', '.join(reorder_items)}")

10 Conclusion

The catalogue audit uses tuple records and integer money calculations to produce a repeatable inventory report. Tests cover one-paise prices, one-digit fractions, exact reorder boundaries, invalid decimal formats, and duplicate IDs following rejected records.
